question: In the pulverized-coal boiler co-firing 20% ammonia, what CO2, CO and NO changes does post-flame ammonia injection give, and what NO change does burnout-zone injection give?
expect: post-flame: CO2 -33%, CO -80%, NO about +88%; burnout zone: NO about +571% (abstract)
rendered:
Based on the document "Ammonia Co-Firing in a Staged-Air Pulverized-Coal Boiler: Reactor-Network Prediction of Carbon Reduction and Nitrogen-Oxide Emissions", post-flame ammonia injection at a 20% ammonia blend results in a reduction of CO2 by 33.0% and CO by 80.47%, and an increase in NO by 87.88%. Burnout-zone injection at the same blend results in a much larger NO penalty, with an increase of about 571% in NO.

Document title: Ammonia Co-Firing in a Staged-Air Pulverized-Coal Boiler: Reactor-Network Prediction of Carbon Reduction and Nitrogen-Oxide Emissions.
